conventions.convention: D² is the closed unit disk. Q_n has q_j=((2j−n−1)/(4(n+1)),0); consequently truncating Q_n does not give the canonical Q_{n−1}. Homeomorphism groups carry the compact-open topology, equal here to uniform convergence.
Mapping-class multiplication is ordinary composition. Representatives fix the boundary pointwise, and isotopies defining Mod preserve the marked set setwise at every time.
PMod is π₀ of the pointwise marked-point stabilizer. Its inclusion into Mod is injective because marked-point permutations are constant along setwise-preserving isotopies.
Configuration-loop multiplication traverses the first loop first. The evaluation boundary sends a loop to the class of the inverse lifted endpoint: δ([α])=[lift(1)⁻¹].

A_ij is the geometric word σ_{j−1}⋯σ_{i+1}σ_i²σ_{i+1}⁻¹⋯σ_{j−1}⁻¹, with the rightmost factor running first. Its PB_n namesake is its image under inverse ordered slicing, so the positive A_in is a clockwise fibre meridian.
For n≥2, α_i=σ_i⋯σ_{n−1}, α_n=1, and x_i=α_{i+1}⁻¹σ_i²α_{i+1}. A written word's first factor is its topmost geometric layer.

The evaluation bundle and its boundary-map consumers assume AC. Smooth point-motion and arc-extension lemmas assume AC_ω. Alexander contraction, local point-motion sections, smoothing of configuration loops, and the explicit planar section are stated choice-free.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let n≥2. At an interior base configuration q and its truncation q′, forgetting the last strand gives 1→F_{n−1}→PB_n→PB_{n−1}→1, where F_{n−1}=π₁(int D²∖{q₁,…,q_{n−1}},q_n) is free on positively oriented puncture meridians and the injection is induced by fibre inclusion, transported to the closed-disk model. PB₁ is trivial.

Assume AC and n≥2. Under the fibre-inclusion identification F_{n−1}≅ker φ, the configuration images of A_{1n},…,A_{n−1,n} form a free basis. There is a compatible system of pairwise interior-disjoint stems such that Ψ([A_in])=(κ_*[γ_i])⁻¹, where γ_i is the counterclockwise based meridian along the i-th stem.

Assume AC. For every n≥0, Ψ=δ∘(ι^C_*)⁻¹∘Φ is a group isomorphism G_n→Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²); each positive geometric half twist maps to its explicit supported boundary-fixed half rotation; every mapping class has a boundary-fixed diffeomorphism representative that is the endpoint of a smooth isotopy from the identity.
Assume AC. The inverse-endpoint boundary map δ:π₁(C_n(int D²),[Q_n])→Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²)=π₀(F) is an isomorphism of groups for every n≥0.

For k∈ℕ and a set Q of k distinct interior disk points, int D²∖Q is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of k circles, with positively oriented puncture meridians forming a free fundamental-group basis, and π_j=0 for every j≥2. At k=0 the wedge is a point. The same conclusions hold for the plane minus k points under the stated radial homeomorphism. No choice axiom is used.

Assume AC and n≥2. If W₁ is an x-word, W₂ uses only σ₁,…,σ_{n−2} and their inverses, and φ(W₁W₂)=1, then φ(x_i)=P_i⁻¹A_inP_i and their PB_n images form a free basis of the forgetful kernel; W₁ freely reduces to the empty x-word; φ(W₂)=1 and φ_{n−1}(W₂)=1.

For n≥3, 1≤i≤n−2 and 1≤j≤n−1, σ_i⁻¹x_jσ_i equals x_j outside j=i,i+1, equals x_{i+1} at j=i, and equals x_{i+1}x_ix_{i+1}⁻¹ at j=i+1. The opposite conjugation equals x_j outside these indices, x_i⁻¹x_{i+1}x_i at j=i, and x_i at j=i+1. These follow using only Artin relations and free moves.

For n≥2, every Artin-letter word with trivial geometric image is equivalent, using only Artin relations and free moves, to W₁W₂, where W₁ uses the abbreviated x-letters and W₂ uses only σ₁,…,σ_{n−2} and their inverses. Either factor may be empty.

concerns.concern: The Statement claims G_t(x)=e^(−2πit)P_t⁻¹(x) preserves Q₂ for an arbitrary evaluation lift P. Step 2.1 infers P_t⁻¹(Q₂)=e^(2πit)Q₂ from P_t(Q₂)=e^(−2πit)Q₂. This inverse-image inference is false without equivariance of P_t with rotations, which is not assumed. Thus the explicitly claimed isotopy need not preserve Q₂, although the general counterexample conclusion is true.

The Statement defines ψ with codomain PMod(D²,Q_{n−1};∂D²) by regarding a map fixing q₁,…,q_n as fixing q₁,…,q_{n−1}. The cited definition fixes canonical Q_m separately for each m; trunc(Q_n)≠Q_{n−1}. Already Q₂=(−1/12,1/12), while Q₁=(0), so the asserted stabilizer inclusion is undefined. Given and steps 1.2/2.1 silently identify these different configurations. An explicit change-of-marked-configuration identification is missing. The batch-21 ledger's verified row against def-boundary-fixed-mapping-class-group-of-a-punctured-disk does not address this mismatch.

The 'Precisely' clause refutes the assertion that every boundary-fixed marked-set-preserving f is 'isotopic rel ∂D² to a homeomorphism that fixes every q_i individually'. As defined in def-boundary-fixed-mapping-class-group-of-a-punctured-disk, an isotopy rel boundary alone may move the marked set; Alexander contraction makes every such f isotopic to the identity. The displayed assertion is therefore true. The missing essential condition is preservation of Q_n setwise throughout the isotopy; without it, the claimed equivalence with PMod=Mod fails.

Step 2.2 sets γ=(α*varsigma)*bar α, but describes its time intervals as first quarter, middle half and last quarter. With the published binary concatenation, these intervals are instead first quarter, second quarter and final half. The displayed ψ₀ and G consequently do not satisfy G(0,t)=γ(t). A reparameterization or a matching piecewise formula closes this gap.

Step 1.4 claims g₁∘ρ^(n)=ρ^(n−1), although g₁ includes translation by h_{n−1}. The relative diamond vectors scale by the linear part of g₁; the displayed equation is false as written. The subsequent equality for full motions is correct after accounting for the midpoint translation.

Step 1.2 claims A∘ρ′=ρ for A(w)=aw−h_n. Relative diamond vectors satisfy aρ′=ρ; composing them with A introduces an extra −h_n. The intended full-motion identity A(m′+ρ′)=m+ρ follows, but the intermediate displayed assertion needs correction.

The 'Relation to the punctured disc' remark says restrictions are isotopic 'as homeomorphisms of the punctured disc exactly when' ambient maps are isotopic rel boundary through marked-set-preserving maps. The restriction-side isotopies need the same pointwise boundary condition explicitly; unrestricted punctured-disk isotopies admit the boundary rotations exhibited on the companion page.

The 'Relation to the punctured disc' paragraph likewise states an unqualified equivalence with isotopies through punctured-disk homeomorphisms. It should specify pointwise boundary fixing throughout. The interval exponential law alone also does not establish extension of punctured-disk isotopies across the missing marked points.

Step 1.3 says 'H₀=H₁ as maps on Q_n', immediately after computing that H₁ exchanges q_i and q_{i+1}. The maps are unequal; only their image sets agree. The following unordered-loop conclusion uses the latter equality.

Step 2.1 calls z:I→F_n(int D²) 'a based loop at [Q_n]'. The point [Q_n] belongs to the unordered quotient, and z may end at a nontrivial permutation of Q_n. z is an ordered path; p∘z is the based loop.
Step 3.1 calls the n=0 evaluation fibration 'the identity map of a contractible space'. Its map is E→C₀(int D²)={point}, with fibre E, rather than id_E. The trivial-group conclusion remains valid.

Step 3.1 says that for n=0 the constant base loop's lift from id 'is constant'. Evaluation is then E→{point}; any path in E starting at id is a lift. One may choose the constant lift, and lift-independence gives the intended class.

Example clause 2 calls the complement of the closed support disk 'a set contained in U_i⊂int D²'. It is the closed support disk that is contained in U_i, not its complement; the Verification states the intended containment correctly.

The purity discussion calls the permutation of σ_{j−1}⋯σ_{i+1} 'a j−i-cycle of the labels i,…,j'. This word fixes label i and cycles i+1,…,j. The purity calculation itself does not use the erroneous label description.
Step 3.1 writes the projection of α*(s′∘γ)*bar α as constant*(s′∘γ)*constant. The middle projected path is γ, not the total-space path s′∘γ; the current displayed equality is ill-typed.

Step 3.1 describes the stem-circle-reversed-stem meridian as 'a simple closed loop'. This based loop retraces its nonempty stem and is not simple. Its circle portion is simple, and the based meridian and free-basis arguments remain valid.
